<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.ui__FormField__visibleOn.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **143** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `92db036a7d81e93e164da603c7d0a690cb5d8a3e` — the merge of head `860f4a18bee5da9ea84a43fb40557d1a5300cd2a` into base `3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 92db036a7d81e93e164da603c7d0a690cb5d8a3e && git checkout 92db036a7d81e93e164da603c7d0a690cb5d8a3e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a 860f4a18bee5da9ea84a43fb40557d1a5300cd2a && git checkout -B drift-repro 3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a && git merge --no-ff 860f4a18bee5da9ea84a43fb40557d1a5300cd2a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3c080a65c8c17af97403fed1c26cddac05f43a6a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept set moved at exactly three positions, and no other.** On `main` the authorable surface declared the two keys at `ui/FormField:visibleOn`, `ui/FormSection:visibleOn` and `ui/PageComponent:visibility` (base `authorable-surface/ui.json` lines 550, 562, 1100) and nowhere else; a key-position sweep of every `*.ts` under `packages/spec/src` at the head finds no fourth predicate-shaped declaration — the other hits are unrelated value keys (marketplace / registry-config / view-switcher `visibility`, the earlier-retired agent `visibility`) or guidance maps that already refuse the spelling (`object.zod.ts:1217`, `app.zod.ts:1088`, `component.zod.ts:894-895`). All three are now `retiredKey()` tombstones (`view.zod.ts:3544`, `:3829`; `page.zod.ts:691`), so the surface rows read `[RETIRED]`. The hunks in `view.zod.ts` and `page.zod.ts` touch only those keys, the section `derivedKeys` list and prose; `derivedKeys` losing `'visibleOn'` is right — the tombstone aborts the section parse before the group-reference refinement runs, which `section-group-reference.test.ts` now pins as exactly one issue at `sections.0.visibleOn`. **Right.**
2. **The prescriptions say what the ruling's letter requires.** Each names `visibleWhen`, the removing release (`@objectstack/spec 18`), ADR-0089 D2, the one-line fix (rename; CEL value unchanged) and the both-written case (delete the old key); the `[REMOVED]` description channel and the parse channel carry the same text (the removal-version pin's `tombstone()` renderer reads both and derives 18 from `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'`). No `os migrate meta` sentence, correctly: `retired-key.ts`'s house sentence binds a surface a chain step replays, and these entries are `toMajor: 15`, below `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR = 16` — the pin's `--from` rule would demand `--from 14`, which `applyMetaMigrations` throws on (`chain.ts`, `MigrationFloorError`). The F5-jsx shape. The `VISIBILITY_STRICT_OPTIONS` prescription no longer offers the two as "still accepted"; `view.test.ts` pins that. **Right.**
3. **The pipes are gone and the parsed output of a `visibleWhen`-only body is unchanged.** `normalizeVisibleWhen` returned its input minus the aliases, so with only `visibleWhen` present the fold was the identity; `FormField` still omits `visibleOn` from the output type; the CONTROL cases in `view.test.ts` and `page.test.ts` pin the canonical output carrying no alias key. Readers of the pipe's input side: the five tests and `buildObjectFormSectionFieldEntry` (`component.zod.ts:6727`) moved to `.shape`; a head-wide grep finds no other hard-coded `.in` read of these three schemas — the remaining `def.in` readers (`component-field-specs-liveness.test.ts`, `protocol.ts:857`, `zod-graph.ts`) branch on `type === 'pipe'` and are unaffected. The dropped-refinements baseline moved 13 sites off `.in` and one site one level shallower (763 → 764), and `check:generated` is green on the head. A slotted page node's `type` refusal now arrives at `slots.header.type` rather than inside an `invalid_union` — a better-located public error shape, pinned in `component.test.ts` and named in the changeset. objectui's `sectionFields.spec-parity.test.ts` reads `SpecFormFieldSchema.in.shape` and is the follow-up card's, as the dev measured. **Right.**
4. **The D3 entry is TRUE against the code.** `applyMetaMigrations` replays only `step.conversionIds` of the hops above `--from` (`chain.ts:218`); the two entries sit in no step (the new test pins `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR` contains neither id), so `os migrate meta --from 17` applies no edit and `--write` writes none; the post-chain refusal listing the entry text describes exists (`migrate/meta.ts:725`, "Migrated stack does not yet pass schema validation"); the entry carries no `relevantWhen`, so it is always listed. Stored rows: `applyConversionsToStoredItem` pins `includeRetired: true` (`stored.ts:107`) and the runner skips a retired entry only when `!includeRetired` (`apply.ts:156`); the protocol's read path routes every non-flow row through it (`protocol.ts:6519`); `visibility-alias-keys-retirement.test.ts` pins a stored view row and a stored page row loading renamed and parsing. The artifact door opens the retired window per entry off `retiredAfter` (`artifact-forward-conversion.ts`, `idsTheFloorPostdates`): a `^17.x` floor on an 18 runtime is `converted-forward` and replays the whole chain; an 18 floor is closed and meets the tombstone — "inside its window" is the exact claim. `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` matches the F1 / F5-jsx / F3 / F2 stamps. **Right.**
5. **The readers — one door is mis-described, and the published text carries the mis-description.** `detectUnboundFormViewPredicateRoots`: its only caller (`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts:1239`) runs it on `result.definition` after `applyArtifactForwardConversions` and only when `FORWARD_WINDOW_OPENED[result.verdict]`; an artifact outside every window answers to the strict parse. `FORM_PREDICATE_KEYS = ['visibleWhen']` loses nothing; pinned end to end in `form-predicate-root-policy.test.ts`. **Right.** `validateVisibilityPredicates` / `validatePredicatePathRefs`: `os validate` (`validate.ts:349` parse, exit before `:530`), `os build` (`compile.ts:408` → `:552`), `os verify` (`judgeAuthorTimeRules`), the per-package pass and the metadata save door (`protocol.ts` parses the `view` / `page` body as submitted, 422 on refusal, and runs `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` after; its canonicalization-before-parse is flow-only) all hand them a parse-accepted body. **`os lint` does not.** `lint.ts:681-683` calls `runAuthoringRules('lint', { normalized: stack, parsed: lowered, … })` where `lowered` is `lowerCallables(stack)`, not a schema parse, and `author-time-rules.ts:82` states it: "`'lint'` never parses — it hands the rules the normalized stack on both tiers". With both D2 entries now `retiredFromLoadPath`, `normalizeStackInput` passes the retired key through — the PR's own pin asserts it (`authoring-rule-input-tier.test.ts`: `expect(JSON.stringify(normalized)).toMatch(/"visibleOn"|"visibility"/)`). So at the `os lint` door a raw `visibleOn` / `visibility` reaches both readers, and neither reads it: a value defect under the retired key — bare identifier, mis-layered root, non-CEL — that 17.7 reported at `os lint` (the live rename, the conversion notice, then the finding; the old premise-3 pin measured exactly that) is now reported nowhere at that door — no notice (entry retired), no refusal (door never parses), no finding (limb dropped). The code is still right by the ruling: item 7 leaves no double spelling, Prime Directive 12 forbids a consumer-side alias read, the two gating doors and strict `defineStack` refuse the key by name, and `os lint`'s standing contract is to judge an unparsed stack where every refused shape is already invisible. What is wrong is the stated mechanism, and it is published: the changeset's `@objectstack/lint` paragraph says "Every door runs them on a body the spec parse accepted, which cannot carry either retired key"; the `CANONICAL` docblock in `validate-visibility-predicates.ts` says "the three CLI commands run the rule stage only after `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` passes (`judgeAuthorTimeRules`)" — `judgeAuthorTimeRules` is `os verify`'s stage, and its own module says the lint door never parses; `validate-predicate-path-refs.ts`'s `PREDICATE_KEYS` docblock, the `authoring-rule-input-tier.test.ts` comment ("the parse every door runs before its rule pass") and the `validate-visibility-predicates.test.ts` describe comment repeat it. The dev's PR body names `judgeAuthorTimeRules`, `run.parsed`, the scaffold door and the save door and never measures `os lint`. This is the F2 class — text that promises what the tool does not do — in a changeset that becomes CHANGELOG text. **Wrong: named defect, below.** `page-envelope-audit.ts` (code unchanged, comments true, the negative control re-pointed to the parse-error channel with a canonical control) and `protocol.ts` (comments only; the graft fixture re-spelled) are **right**. `packages/sdui-parser/src/validate.ts` unchanged is acceptable: `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` is objectui's node vocabulary, not `PageComponentSchema`, and moves with the objectui card.
6. **The kept exports' docblock is true.** A head-wide grep finds no caller of `normalizeVisibleWhen` or `VISIBILITY_ALIAS_KEYS` outside `visibility.ts` (only the api-surface / export-origins listings and prose); "no schema in this package calls the fold any more" and "remain published, with no caller in this repository" hold. The acceptance note is also true: `18.visibility-strict-options-unexported.ts` says the two "stay exported", so retiring them is a separate decision that rewrites that entry. Three analogy mentions survive outside the diff (`view.zod.ts:3949`, `public-auth-features.ts:321`, and a stale "fold them via" in `visible-when-alias-guidance.test.ts:297`); none is load-bearing — the last may ride the patch round. **Right.**
7. **Re-pointed suites and the verdict-list pin.** `conversions.test.ts` keeps exactly `flow-node-http-callout-rename` and lists the two among the retired with the stamp; `view-spelling-walk.test.ts` gains the retired-but-replayed statement; the removal-version `JOIN` gains the three tombstone rows; no suite outside the stored seam still drives either entry as a live subject (head-wide grep).
